summary: Jackson County lookout on Wagner Butte: tent camp 1913 or rag camp 1915, cupola cabin 1923, R-6 cab 1961, burned or removed 1971. Foundations and a railing remain.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (1923), then a prefabricated R-6 flat cab (1961)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or burned in 1971; the foundations and a metal railing remain

access.note: National Forest trail; the trail page advises against stock because crossing a landslide area is difficult

visit.trail_note: Trail #1011 begins on Forest Road 22; the last stretch is a short scramble over large boulders

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Crater then Rogue River National Forest

events.note: Tent camp and Osborne alidade established, per Oregon Hikers and Forest Lookouts; the register dates a rag camp to 1915
Osborne fire-finder on the summit; the observer had to climb down the rocks to the telephone to report a fire
Observer on the summit for the Forest Service
Summit leveled with explosives; D-6 cupola cabin, the first permanent structure, finished in October

Fire reported from the lookout and completely out by 9 p.m. that day
Lightning struck 500 yards from the lookout station
Old cabin dismantled; prefabricated R-6 flat cab about 15 feet square built, concrete flown in by helicopter
Forest Lookouts history lists the lookout as discontinued
Intentionally burned by smokejumpers, per Oregon Hikers; the register says removed and firelookout.com says destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Oregon Hikers and Forest Lookouts date a tent camp to 1913; the register dates a rag camp to 1915. Both are reported; the 1923 cupola cabin is agreed by all sources.

The register and the Forest Service trail page say removed (1971 and the 1970s); firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971; Oregon Hikers says smokejumpers burned it on purpose in 1971. The story reports the disagreement.
Forest Lookouts lists the lookout as discontinued in 1964, while the cab is dated to 1971 by three sources. No source says when staffing ended, so the story gives both without reconciling them.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 4.6 is not supported by any source. The only size given for the 1961 cab is about 15 feet square (Forest Lookouts), which may be the origin of the 4.6 m figure (15 ft is about 4.6 m); it is left out of facts for review. The Everything Mountains page cited in a search snippet returned only an empty directory listing, so its footings claim is not used; the footings and railing are taken from Oregon Hikers. Grokipedia and the cherylhill.net blog were not cited. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with public, based on the National Forest trail. The fact-check rewrote sentences that copied quote wording and added quote evidence for the dates the story gives; no date or fact in the story was found to be wrong.
